meta.description: Controls error rates across thousands of simultaneous tests in genomics discovery using false-discovery-rate methods (Benjamini-Hochberg, Benjamini-Yekutieli, Storey q-value with pi0 estimation, local FDR, independent filtering, covariate-weighted FDR via IHW), plus family-wise error control (Bonferroni, Holm) and the GWAS genome-wide threshold. Use when correcting p-values from genome-wide tests, choosing between BH/BY/q-value/Bonferroni, setting an FDR threshold, applying IHW or independent filtering, or interpreting q-values.
meta.environment: R 4.4.3 / Bioconductor 3.20 (qvalue 2.38.0, IHW 1.34.0, limma 3.62.2, DESeq2 1.46.0, edgeR 4.4.2); Python 3.12 (statsmodels 0.15.0, scipy 1.18.1, numpy 2.5.3, pandas 3.0.5). All installed versions meet or exceed the skill's stated Version Compatibility floors (qvalue 2.34+, IHW 1.30+, statsmodels 0.14+, scipy 1.12+), so no result here is attributable to a version gap. All data is SYNTHETIC with planted ground truth.

scientific_integrity.detail: Nine primary citations, all with real journal/volume/page coordinates and no invented DOI or PMID. The two quantitative claims that could be tested offline both held: statsmodels multipletests really does default to method='hs' (verified from the installed signature and by rejection counts, 60 vs 300), and the GWAS 5e-8 / Dudbridge-Gusnanto 7.2e-8 pairing is stated correctly. No numeric result in the skill was fabricated.

practice_boundaries.detail: Nothing in the skill or in any of the seven outputs diagnoses, prescribes or triages an individual. The one clinical input (Input 6, four pre-specified trial endpoints) is handled purely as a population-level error-rate question and is routed to clinical-biostatistics/multiplicity-graphical. Gate 7 (research scope) is clean.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled fallacy. The FDR-versus-FWER framing, the PRDS condition, pi0 estimation, the filter-independence rule and the false-coverage-rate trap are all stated correctly and three of them were confirmed against planted truth. Two claims are miscalibrated rather than wrong -- the 'realized FDR exceeds nominal' symptom for BH under negative dependence (not reproduced in 400 replicates) and the grouping of variance filtering with preliminary-test filtering (measured null-independent) -- and are raised as P1/P2, not as a veto.

code_usability.detail: The p.adjust, qvalue, statsmodels and Bonferroni/Holm/BY patterns all executed and produced correct results, and the shipped examples/multiple_testing_correction.R ran to completion (exit 0). The SKILL.md IHW call crashed the R session (SIGSEGV in the lpsymphony backend) in 2 of 3 attempts at 18,000 genes, but a documented-API variant of the same call (positional form, nbins <= 5) runs and returns correct results, so the code is not unrunnable in the M4 sense. Recorded as P1, not vetoed.

functional_suitability.note: Approach is well matched: one-line patterns for a decision problem, with execution correctly delegated to sibling skills. Correctness is high and verifiable. The gap is completeness -- the frontmatter description promises local FDR, independent filtering, the false-coverage-rate fix and IDR, but IDR is one taxonomy row with no code or package guidance, FCR is named four times with no formula, and local FDR is one assignment with no interpretation rule.

reliability.note: Per-Method Failure Modes covers Bonferroni, BH-under-dependence, the statsmodels default, filtering and FCR with trigger/mechanism/symptom/fix. The two methods the skill most actively promotes as power levers, q-value and IHW, are the only ones with no entry -- and both are exactly what failed in execution. The Version Compatibility recovery protocol is real but assumes a catchable error, which a segfault is not. Category 3 Scene Overrides applied: no deduction taken for strict input handling.

performance_context.note: 192 lines carrying a taxonomy, a scenario decision tree, a reconciliation table, five failure modes and nine citations, with no filler; workflow is one-liners with no redundant round-trips. Minor: there is no references/ directory to defer depth into, so everything loads at once, though the total is small enough that this costs little.

agent_usability.note: Strongest category. The decision tree and taxonomy let an agent route correctly from a cold start, terminology is consistent throughout, and error prevention is unusually concrete for a statistics skill. Deductions: the IHW snippet references a de_table that is never defined, and no output shape is specified beyond 'report the adjusted quantity with its interpretation'. goal_approach_exempt: true is honoured -- no deduction for absent Goal/Approach blocks.

human_usability.note: Discoverability is excellent: the description uses the phrasings analysts actually type and the usage guide supplies eight realistic prompts. Forgiveness scored under the Category 3 override on documented requirements rather than strictness -- the skill states no input requirements at all, and its q-value one-liner has no documented family-size floor, which is where it breaks.

security.note: No credentials, no network calls, no shell execution, no eval/exec, no destructive operations, and the skill only ever touches summary statistics. The deduction is input validation: the central correctness condition of the skill is an independence assumption (IHW covariate, filter statistic) and it ships no diagnostic for testing it, nor any instruction to check that p-values are valid.

maintainability.note: Clean section separation, table-driven content that extends easily, and explicit delegation boundaries. Testability is the weak point: the single shipped example is seeded and runnable, but with its own seed it prints a realized FDR of 0.108 for BH at nominal 0.05 and an IHW result identical to BH, so the only test artifact actively teaches the wrong lesson.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision, composability, idempotency and escape hatches are all at full marks -- seven qualified sibling paths, every one of which exists in the repository, and three separate routings out of the confirmatory-trial case. The single deduction is progressive disclosure: examples/multiple_testing_correction.R is never mentioned by SKILL.md or usage-guide.md, so an agent has no reason to open it.

recommendations.title: IHW is a headline power lever with no failure-mode coverage
recommendations.problem: The exact call printed in SKILL.md, ihw(pvalue ~ mean_expression, data = de_table, alpha = 0.05), segfaulted the R session in 2 of 3 attempts on an 18,000-gene table under IHW 1.34.0 / R 4.4.3 / Bioconductor 3.20; the positional form from examples/ also crashed at default nbins for m >= 8000, and only nbins <= 5 was stable at 18,000 genes. The failure kills the interpreter, so nothing the analyst can catch is raised.
recommendations.root_cause: The Per-Method Failure Modes section covers Bonferroni, BH, statsmodels, filtering and FCR but has no entry for IHW, so there is no documented fallback, no nbins guidance, no mention of the lpsymphony LP backend the method depends on, and no note that IHW silently reduces to Benjamini-Hochberg when the bin count collapses (which it printed at m = 2000).
recommendations.fix: Add an IHW failure-mode block: name the lpsymphony/Rsymphony solver dependency, give nbins as the first parameter to reduce when the call fails or hangs, note the built-in 'more than 1000 p-values' guard, and instruct a documented fall back to plain BH with the power loss stated when IHW cannot be made to run.

recommendations.title: The q-value one-liner is unreliable on small families and pi0 is unstable there
recommendations.problem: qvalue(pvalues) as printed failed with 'Error in smooth.spline(lambda, pi0, df = smooth.df): missing or infinite values in inputs are not allowed' in 178 of 500 all-null families at m = 20 and 35 of 500 at m = 50. Where it did return, pi0-hat fell as low as 0.301 against a planted truth of 1.0 at m = 50 and 0.376 at m = 100, so the number the skill tells the analyst to report can be badly wrong on small families.
recommendations.root_cause: The q-value section presents a bare one-liner with no minimum family size and never mentions the lambda or pi0.method arguments that govern the spline fit which is what actually breaks.
recommendations.fix: State a working floor in the q-value section (pi0 estimation needs a family in the thousands), show qvalue(p, pi0.method = 'bootstrap') and qvalue(p, lambda = 0) as the documented fallbacks, and add a q-value entry to Per-Method Failure Modes with the smooth.spline error as its symptom.

recommendations.title: The BH-to-BY rule prescribes a large power loss on an undiagnosable symptom
recommendations.problem: Across 1,200 replicate datasets BH never lost FDR control: mean realized FDP was 0.0444 under independence, 0.0393 under strong positive block dependence (rho = 0.8) and 0.0453 under pairwise negative dependence at rho = -0.95. The stated symptom, 'realized FDR exceeds nominal', never appeared -- and could not be observed by a real analyst in any case. Meanwhile switching to BY cost 53% of power (0.605 to 0.288) and more than half the rejections (312 to 141).
recommendations.root_cause: The failure-mode entry presents a worst-case theoretical guarantee as an observable symptom, and the decision tree converts it into an unconditional recommendation for 'strong/unknown/negative dependence', which sweeps in the common case of merely unknown dependence.
recommendations.fix: Replace the symptom line with what dependence actually does -- under positive block dependence the FDP standard deviation rose from 0.011 to 0.043 and the chance of FDP exceeding 0.10 went from 0.000 to 0.092 while the mean stayed controlled -- quantify BY's power cost, and narrow the decision-tree row to cases where negative dependence is actually expected rather than merely unestablished.

recommendations.title: The false-coverage-rate fix is named four times and shipped nowhere
recommendations.problem: The decision tree, the Per-Method Failure Modes block and the Common Errors table all end at 'FCR-adjusted intervals for the selected set', but no formula, package or worked example exists anywhere in the skill, so a routine request for confidence intervals on the reported hits cannot be completed from it. The gap is not cosmetic: naive 95% intervals on the BH-0.05 selected set covered the true effect only 82.4% of the time, and the Benjamini-Yekutieli 2005 construction restored 97.6%, but had to be written from the primary literature.
recommendations.root_cause: FCR is treated as a caution to be raised rather than a procedure to be executed, unlike BH, BY, q-value and IHW which all get code.
recommendations.fix: Add a short code block computing the FCR-adjusted level as 1 - alpha*R/m and applying it to the selected set, alongside the Benjamini & Yekutieli 2005 citation, so the warning ends in an action the way the other failure modes do.

recommendations.title: The shipped example teaches the wrong lesson twice
recommendations.problem: Run as shipped, examples/multiple_testing_correction.R prints a realized FDR of 0.108 for BH at a nominal 0.05 -- the 99.7th percentile of that same simulation's FDP distribution over 300 seeds, whose mean is 0.0472 -- so every reader sees the recommended method apparently failing by a factor of two. Its IHW section then prints 'IHW discoveries at FDR 0.05 = 93 (vs BH = 93)', zero gain, for a section whose stated purpose is that IHW 'recovers power vs plain BH'; the same rgamma covariate on the audit data gave 196 against BH's 204, an outright loss.
recommendations.root_cause: The seed was never checked against the distribution it draws from, and the demo covariate satisfies only the null-independence half of the IHW precondition while carrying no information about power, which is the other half.
recommendations.fix: Average the method-comparison table over replicates, or pick a seed near the median of the FDP distribution; and generate the IHW covariate so power genuinely depends on it (for example tie per-gene noise to mean expression, which produced a 17% discovery gain here) so the section demonstrates the effect it claims.

recommendations.title: The filtering rule is right but names the wrong instance
recommendations.problem: The skill groups 'a pre-test on variance' with 'a preliminary t-test' as filters that are not null-independent and bias the FDR anti-conservatively. Measured over 200 replicates, the preliminary t-test behaved exactly as described (null p<0.05 rate 0.1001, mean FDP 0.0831, alpha exceeded in 86.7% of replicates), but group-blind variance filtering left the null p-value rate at 0.0502 against a 0.0500 target and doubled power, and within-group variance biased p-values conservatively (0.0138) rather than anti-conservatively. Following the skill's mean-only prescription on this data halved power, from 0.105 to 0.055.
recommendations.root_cause: One sentence collapses three filter statistics with three different behaviours into a single warning, and the allow-list contains exactly one entry (overall mean count) borrowed from the count-data setting where a mean-variance trend makes it informative.
recommendations.fix: Name the statistics separately with the direction of each bias, say that the mean filter buys power only where mean predicts power, and add the one-line diagnostic used here -- check that null p-values stay uniform within strata of the filter statistic -- so an analyst can test any proposed filter instead of consulting a two-item list.

recommendations.title: Three advertised topics appear only as taxonomy rows
recommendations.problem: The frontmatter description promises local FDR, independent filtering and reproducibility ranking via IDR. In the body, IDR is a single taxonomy row naming an unspecified 'idr (ENCODE)' package with no code and no citation link in the workflow, and local FDR is one assignment, qobj$lfdr, with no cutoff, no interpretation rule and no statement of how it relates to the q-value threshold. Choosing a cutoff of 0.20 arbitrarily returned 364 features at a realized FDP of 0.0934, which no guidance in the skill would have predicted or sanctioned.
recommendations.root_cause: The description was written to the full breadth of the topic while the body was written to the four methods that carry code, leaving a gap between what triggers the skill and what it can do.
recommendations.fix: Either add one sentence each giving a conventional lfdr cutoff with the per-feature-versus-tail-average distinction, and a concrete IDR entry point, or trim those promises out of the description so the trigger matches the content.
